claims.text: Low hardness and strength in equimolar CoCrFeNiTi result from an enhanced rate of dynamic dislocation recovery.
Ti introduces only modest lattice distortion in simple-solid-solution CoCrFeNiTi.
The modest lattice distortion associated with Ti produces low lattice friction.
Low lattice friction facilitates extensive dislocation cross-slip and rearrangement.
Dislocation cross-slip and rearrangement prevent formation of a hardened dislocation network.
Low dislocation pile-ups, extensive glide and cross-slip, and rapid rearrangement into low-energy configurations are indicators of dynamic recovery.
Dynamic recovery occurs during the early stages of plastic deformation in CoCrFeNiTi.
Dynamic recovery minimizes forest hardening in CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti-free CoCrFeNi has greater solute pinning than CoCrFeNiTi.
Greater solute pinning in CoCrFeNi causes greater dislocation accumulation and strength.
At room temperature and moderate strain rates, CoCrFeNiTi will have a lower work-hardening rate than identically processed CoCrFeNi.
At room temperature and moderate strain rates, CoCrFeNiTi will accumulate fewer dislocations than identically processed CoCrFeNi.
Cryogenic temperature or very high strain rate will inhibit dynamic recovery in CoCrFeNiTi.
When dynamic recovery is inhibited, dislocation accumulation in CoCrFeNiTi will match or exceed that in CoCrFeNi.
When dynamic recovery is inhibited, the hardness of CoCrFeNiTi will match or exceed that of CoCrFeNi.
Identically processed CoCrFeNi is expected to have marginally higher hardness and strength because its dynamic recovery rate is lower.

The proposed mechanism is bounded to equimolar CoCrFeNiTi and CoCrFeNi in simple solid-solution states under tensile or compression loading at room or cryogenic temperatures and moderate-to-high strain rates.
Failure to observe lower room-temperature work hardening and dislocation accumulation in CoCrFeNiTi relative to CoCrFeNi would falsify the proposed dominant-recovery mechanism.
Failure of cryogenic recovery suppression to increase dislocation density and hardness in CoCrFeNiTi would falsify the proposed dominant-recovery mechanism.

contradictions.description: The alloys cannot literally have identical solute distributions because one is equimolar CoCrFeNiTi and the other is Ti-free CoCrFeNi. The intended control may be identical distributional homogeneity or segregation state, but that qualification is not stated.
